question: When braking begins during the first sparse wake, can any continuously tracked vortex loop survive without further work, including after the obstacle potential is removed? How do the results transfer across time step, spatial grid and box extent when time integration preserves the norm?
prior_access: The later-stop C++ outcomes informed the early schedule. In the first early-stop run, independently recomputed prefixes had unequal SHA-256 despite identical initial hashes, signed plaquettes and saved density slices for the base seeds. Budget differences before intervention were small. Outcomes after intervention were not used to choose new thresholds, conditions, or seeds. This plan reuses the schedules and seeds to correct the failed pairing.
independent_unit: Three seeded shared histories from t=0, each forked at the prespecified time with byte-identical fields. All continuations of one seed share a preparation. The held and release arms also share one brake trajectory through t=70. Precision and extent variants repeat seed 92301.
inputs: The dimensionless rubidium bulk-scale Gross–Pitaevskii equation with gamma=0 and the same discrete Laplacian as the preceding experiment. Start with constant density and a small seeded phase modulation. The obstacle ramps and accelerates as before. Continue at 0.68 c, or brake over t=58..70; a third arm switches the stationary potential off smoothly from t=70 to t=82. No ring is present at t=0. The snapshot at t=58 and the stopped snapshot at t=70 are copied as-is without normalizing, rotating or editing the field.
measurement: Save signed nonzero phase windings, density slices, energy, work, mass and same-time prefix hashes. Use the original component and one-to-one association criteria. Cohort eligible with continuous associations from t=54 to t=58. Report at t=70,82,120,160 and count new sustained track starts after t=82; use V cutoffs 0.25,0.5,1 and temporal decimation by two. Track endpoints mean last observable association. Report final and peak energy residuals and mass drift. Plot the declared seed 92301 only.
alternatives: The held-potential arm measures a stationary obstacle with zero work after t=70. The release arm controls whether the held potential is needed: it permits signed work during the fade but V and its time derivative vanish thereafter. Compare ongoing work, remaining energy and previous wake. Same time step, spatial or extent variants check transfer. Finite periodic images and internal stored motion remain present. This corrective run uses bytes carried forward from the single common computation; it does not test whether separate FFT invocations are always bitwise identical. The full first invocation is retained separately.
stopping: Every listed case from t=0 to 160, output every 2 units and common images at 0,58,70,82,120,160. Record all completion states and any failure diagnostics. No result-based stopping.

protocol.software: NumPy float64/complex128, SciPy pocketfft workers=1 in each history. Strang split time step with exact phase and periodic kinetic update and the external potential at the midpoint. Work integrated by endpoint trapezoid.
